Improved Neighbors' k-core

Source: R/centrality-batch52.R
centrality_ink.Rd

The improved neighbors' k-core (INK; Lin et al. 2014) sums a power of the core number of every neighbor of a node: $$S(i) = \sum_{j \in J(i)} k_s(j)^{\alpha},$$ where \(k_s(j)\) is the core number of \(j\) in the whole network and \(J(i)\) is the set of neighbors of \(i\). It separates nodes that share the same core number by the cores their neighbors belong to.

Usage

centrality_ink(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses ink_alpha (the exponent \(\alpha\), default 1).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The node's own core number is not part of its sum. Scores are raw sums. Isolated nodes score 0, the empty sum.

With ink_alpha = 0 the score is the degree. With ink_alpha = 1, the default, it is the sum of the neighbors' core numbers, which is the neighborhood coreness of Bae and Kim (2014). The default is the value Lin et al. use in their experiments. They report that the best-performing exponent depends on the network (0.7, 1, 2.4 and 5 on their four networks). Values above one give more weight to neighbors in high cores, and values below one give less.

A negative ink_alpha, which the source does not define, raises a cograph_bad_parameter error, and so does an exponent so large that a core number raised to it is not a finite number. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Lin, J.-H., Guo, Q., Dong, W.-Z., Tang, L.-Y. and Liu, J.-G. (2014). Identifying the node spreading influence with largest k-core values. Physics Letters A, 378(45), 3279-3284. doi:10.1016/j.physleta.2014.09.054 .

Bae, J. and Kim, S. (2014). Identifying and ranking influential spreaders in complex networks by neighborhood coreness. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 395, 549-559. doi:10.1016/j.physa.2013.10.047 .

See also

centrality_extended_coreness, centrality_coreness, centrality.

Examples

centrality_ink(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>         20         24         28         24         20         20         16 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>         20         24         20 
centrality_ink(regulation_net, ink_alpha = 2)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>         80         96        112         96         80         80         64 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>         80         96         80
